items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: I was acquainted with Fats, and he wanted me to come in on the band for awhile. I did, I did about three or four weeks down there with him

ctx.x: and you get from work and you see the musicians in the band and you hear them, and nobody bothered you then. You wasn't held up or nothing in the streets. Everybody could walk along the streets any time of night, just carefree.

And I'd been there and all like that, and I was acquainted with Fats, and he wanted me to come in on the band for awhile. I did, I did about three or four weeks down there with him, but I didn't like the downstairs. I was more used to Broadway, I didn't like working up there. This was different from Connie's Inn, Connie's Inn was sedate and all like that, and the Capital was a little more honkytonk and stuff.
I didn't care for it, so I got away from it. But I liked Fats, he was great. You know, that guy, they had to put a new piano in there about every two or three months, he was so heavy-handed.
